First: the bright one. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

Second: the blazing one. This was said by Mujahid.

Third: the one that diminishes (or extinguishes). This was said by Ikrima.

Fourth: that the piercing star is the one that has risen above all the stars. This was said by al-Farra' (Yahya ibn Ziyad, the grammarian).

Fifth: the piercing one is the devils when they are pelted. This was said by al-Suddi.

Sixth: the piercing one in its course and its orbit. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Concerning this piercing star there are two views:

One: that it is Saturn. This was said by Ali.

The other: that it is the Pleiades. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

His saying: ﴿There is no soul but that it has a guardian over it﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: "lamma" means "illa" (except), and the meaning is: "There is no soul except that a guardian is over it." This was said by Qatada.

The other: that "ma" after the lam is an extra (zaʾida) particle, and the meaning is: "Indeed every soul has a guardian over it." This was said by al-Akhfash.

Concerning the guardian there are two views:

One: a guardian from Allah who protects over him his term and his provision. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

The other: from the angels who record over him his deeds, good or evil. This was said by Qatada.

It may also carry a third meaning: that the guardian over him is his intellect, for it guides him to his welfare and restrains him from harm.

His saying: ﴿He is created from a gushing fluid, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: from between the man's backbone and his ribs. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatada.

[p-247]

The other: meaning the loins of men and the ribs of women.

Concerning al-taraʾib (the ribs/breastbones) there are six sayings:

First: that it is the chest. This was said by Ibn Iyad, and from it is the saying of Durayd ibn al-Simma:

If you turn your backs, we will seize you by your backs, and if you advance, we will seize you by the breastbones.

Second: what is between the two shoulders to the chest. This was said by Mujahid.

Third: the place of the necklace. This was said by Ibn Abbas. The poet said:

And saffron upon her breastbones; the throat and the neck were drenched with it.

Fourth: that they are four ribs on the lower side. This was said by Ibn Jubayr. al-Zajjaj related that the taraʾib are four ribs on the right side of the chest and four ribs on the left side of the chest.

Fifth: that they are between the two hands, the two feet and the two eyes. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Sixth: that they are the essence of the heart. This was said by Maʿmar ibn Abi Habiba.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him﴾. Concerning this there are five meanings:

First: that He is able to return the semen into the urethra. This was said by Mujahid.

Second: that He is able to return the water into the loins. This was said by Ikrima.

Third: that He is able to return a person from old age to youth, from youth to childhood, and from childhood to the drop (of semen). This was said by al-Dahhak.

Fourth: that He is able to restore him to life after his death. This was said by al-Hasan, Ikrima and Qatada.

Fifth: that He is able to hold back the water so that it does not come out.

It may also carry a sixth meaning: that He is able to return him to this world after his resurrection in the Hereafter, because the disbelievers will ask Allah for a return to it.

His saying: ﴿On the Day when secrets are laid bare﴾, meaning: they will be made manifest.

It may also carry a second meaning: that they will be tested by the manifestation of hidden things in the Hereafter after they were concealed in this world.

Concerning it there are two views:

[p-248]

One: everything a person has concealed of good or evil, and what he harboured of faith or disbelief. As al-Ahwas said:

Your secret of affection will be tested in the hidden depths of the heart and the inner parts, on the day when secrets are laid bare.

The other: what Khalid related from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The trusts are three: prayer, fasting, and major ritual impurity (janaba). Allah entrusts the son of Adam with prayer; if he wishes he says, 'I have prayed,' though he has not prayed. Allah entrusts the son of Adam with fasting; if he wishes he says, 'I have fasted,' though he has not fasted. Allah entrusts the son of Adam with janaba; if he wishes he says, 'I have bathed,' though he has not bathed." Recite, if you wish: ﴿On the Day when secrets are laid bare﴾.

His saying: ﴿Then he will have no power nor any helper﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: that the power is the clan, and the helper is the ally. This was said by Sufyan.

The other: he will have no power in his body, nor any helper from others by whom he can defend himself against Allah or by whom he can gain victory over Allah. This is the meaning of Qatada's saying.

It may also carry a third meaning: he will have no power to resist, nor any helper in argument.

﴿By the sky of the returning rain﴾. On this there are four opinions. The first is that it refers to rain, because it returns every year. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is that it refers to clouds, because they bring back the rain.

The third is that it refers to the return to what it was, said by 'Ikrimah.

The fourth is that it refers to the returning stars, said by Ibn Zayd.

It may also be understood as a fifth: the angels, because the deeds of the servants return to them. This is an oath.(p-249)

﴿And by the earth that splits open﴾. On this there are four opinions. The first is that it refers to plants, because the earth splits open to bring them forth. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is that it refers to valleys, because the earth has split open through them. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

The third is that it refers to the paths that are split open by people walking on them. This was said by Mujahid.

The fourth is that it refers to farmland, because it is split open by ploughing.

It may also be understood as a fifth: the dead, because they split open from their graves for the Resurrection. These two are oaths. ﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word﴾. On this the oath falls. Regarding the meaning of "a decisive word" there are two opinions:

The first is what He mentioned earlier of the threat, in His words: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him﴾ and ﴿On the Day when secrets are tested﴾, up to the end of the verse, confirming His threat. According to this, regarding the interpretation of His words "decisive" (fasl), there are two views: the first is "a limit (hadd)", said by Ibn Jubayr; the second is "justice ('adl)", said by al-Dahhak.

The second opinion is that the intended "decisive word" is the Qur'an, confirming His Book. According to this, regarding the interpretation of His words "decisive" there are two views:

The first is "truth (haqq)", said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is what al-Harith narrated from 'Ali, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Book of Allah contains the best of what came before you and the judgement of what comes after you. It is the decisive word, not a jest. Whoever abandons it out of arrogance, Allah will break him. Whoever seeks guidance in other than it, Allah will lead him astray." ﴿And it is not a jest﴾. This is the completion of what the oath falls upon. On this phrase there are three views:

The first is "with play", said by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

The second is "with falsehood", said by Waki' and al-Dahhak.

The third is "with lying", said by al-Suddi.

﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot﴾. He means the people of Makkah when they gathered in the Assembly House (Dar al-Nadwa) to scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you or kill you or expel you﴾. Here He said: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot﴾, meaning they are devising a scheme.(p-250)

﴿And I too am plotting a plot﴾. He means by retribution: in the Hereafter with the Fire, and in this world with the sword.

﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; grant them respite gradually﴾. On "ruwaydan" there are three views:

The first is "near", said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is "waiting", and from this is the poet's saying:

"Wait patiently until the haze of this shining cloud clears and is gone."

The third is "a little", said by Qatada.

Al-Dahhak said: They were killed on the Day of Badr.

Regarding "mahhala" and "amhala" there are two views:

The first is that they are two dialects with one meaning.

The second is that their meanings differ: "mahhala" means to hold back from them, while "amhala" means waiting for punishment to befall them.

The second is that it refers to valleys, because the earth has split open through them. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

The third is that it refers to the paths that are split open by people walking on them. This was said by Mujahid.

The fourth is that it refers to farmland, because it is split open by ploughing.

It may also be understood as a fifth: the dead, because they split open from their graves for the Resurrection. These two are oaths. ﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word﴾. On this the oath falls. Regarding the meaning of "a decisive word" there are two opinions:

The first is what He mentioned earlier of the threat, in His words: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him﴾ and ﴿On the Day when secrets are tested﴾, up to the end of the verse, confirming His threat. According to this, regarding the interpretation of His words "decisive" (fasl), there are two views: the first is "a limit (hadd)", said by Ibn Jubayr; the second is "justice ('adl)", said by al-Dahhak.

The second opinion is that the intended "decisive word" is the Qur'an, confirming His Book. According to this, regarding the interpretation of His words "decisive" there are two views:

The first is "truth (haqq)", said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is what al-Harith narrated from 'Ali, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Book of Allah contains the best of what came before you and the judgement of what comes after you. It is the decisive word, not a jest. Whoever abandons it out of arrogance, Allah will break him. Whoever seeks guidance in other than it, Allah will lead him astray." ﴿And it is not a jest﴾. This is the completion of what the oath falls upon. On this phrase there are three views:

The first is "with play", said by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

The second is "with falsehood", said by Waki' and al-Dahhak.

The third is "with lying", said by al-Suddi.

﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot﴾. He means the people of Makkah when they gathered in the Assembly House (Dar al-Nadwa) to scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you or kill you or expel you﴾. Here He said: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot﴾, meaning they are devising a scheme.(p-250)

﴿And I too am plotting a plot﴾. He means by retribution: in the Hereafter with the Fire, and in this world with the sword.

﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; grant them respite gradually﴾. On "ruwaydan" there are three views:

The first is "near", said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second is "waiting", and from this is the poet's saying:

"Wait patiently until the haze of this shining cloud clears and is gone."

The third is "a little", said by Qatada.

Al-Dahhak said: They were killed on the Day of Badr.

Regarding "mahhala" and "amhala" there are two views:

The first is that they are two dialects with one meaning.

The second is that their meanings differ: "mahhala" means to hold back from them, while "amhala" means waiting for punishment to befall them.
